advances: For every finite complete globally affine lattice law, arithmetic log-rank bounds the intrinsic dimensions of all exact weight levels simultaneously. Their zero-score reflected rows therefore yield a general original-mass energy criterion with no parity-occupancy hypothesis. The exact product energy pays the halfspace coefficient once for the whole product. In particular every four-level factor of arithmetic rank at least two meets the ambient energy threshold, even without the parity restriction in the accepted three-weight theorem. This is a sufficient criterion on a restricted class, not the all-support moment hypothesis required by the locked-target consumer.

proof:
All probabilities below are the original \(w_x/Z\). The hats in (2) have exactly the same meaning and normalization as in accepted fact 4e2de5c00a49d7b9. We prove the intrinsic estimate directly, so its parity-occupancy and spectral-gap assumptions are not invoked.

First, \(\Gamma\) is a free abelian group of rank \(h\). Indeed, every subgroup of \(\mathbb Z^n\) is free abelian: induction on the number of coordinates, projection onto one coordinate, and a lift of a generator of the nonzero cyclic image split the group into that cyclic group and the projection kernel. The rank of integer difference vectors agrees over \(\mathbb Q\) and \(\mathbb R\), by the nonzero minors of their matrix, so the rank of \(\Gamma\) is \(h\).

The homomorphism \(v\mapsto\boldsymbol\ell\cdot v\) has image generated by the finitely many numbers \(\log(w_x/w_{a_0})\). Its rational rank is exactly \(r\). Let
$$
\Gamma_0=\lbrace v\in\Gamma:\boldsymbol\ell\cdot v=0\rbrace.
$$
Extending this homomorphism \(\mathbb Q\)-linearly to \(\Gamma\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q\) gives a map of rational rank \(r\). Its kernel is \(\Gamma_0\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q\): a rational vector in the kernel can be multiplied by a positive integer into \(\Gamma_0\). Rank-nullity therefore gives \(\operatorname{rank}\Gamma_0=h-r\). This also proves \(0\le r\le h\). The kernel is saturated in \(\Gamma\), since \(t\boldsymbol\ell\cdot v=0\), for a nonzero integer \(t\), implies \(\boldsymbol\ell\cdot v=0\). Neither assertion says that \(\Gamma\) or \(\Gamma_0\) is saturated in an ambient integer lattice.

For any two points in the same exact weight level, their difference belongs to \(\Gamma_0\). Thus the real span of all differences in level \(A_k\) is contained in the real span of \(\Gamma_0\). The latter has dimension \(h-r\), again because the group consists of integer vectors. Hence \(h_k\le h-r\). This is the general kernel argument whose special arithmetic-rank use in 1208ab7bdf43319c concerned one exact threshold tree. It does not identify the rational rank \(r\) with the real rank of the original single functional.

Fix a level \(A_k\), choose \(a_k\in A_k\), and set
$$
V_k=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}(A_k-a_k),\qquad
\mathcal L_k=V_k\cap\mathbb Z^n.
$$
This is the saturated intrinsic lattice of the level, and its rank is \(h_k\). The rank assertion follows because \(V_k\) is spanned by integer vectors and the ranks over \(\mathbb Q\) and \(\mathbb R\) agree. In particular \(\mathcal L_k/2\mathcal L_k\) has exactly \(2^{h_k}\) elements. We use this lattice for parity counting, rather than replacing it by the possibly nonsaturated group generated by level differences.

The exact level is complete in its intrinsic affine lattice:
$$
A_k=\operatorname{conv}(A_k)\cap(a_k+\mathcal L_k).
\tag{10}
$$
For a point on the right, membership in \(Q\cap\mathbb Z^n=A\) follows from convexity, and its affine log weight equals the common log weight of the level. Thus it lies in \(A_k\). The reverse inclusion is immediate. For \(x,y\in a_k+\mathcal L_k\), their midpoint is an integer point if and only if \(x-y\in2\mathcal L_k\). For the nontrivial direction, an integral midpoint makes \((x-y)/2\) an integer vector in \(V_k\), hence an element of \(\mathcal L_k\). Consequently every ordered pair in one intrinsic parity class of \(A_k\) has its midpoint in \(A_k\), by (10).

Let \(M_k=|A_k|\), let \(t_k\) be the common original atom probability on that level, and let \(M_{k,u}\) count its points in intrinsic parity class \(u\in\mathcal L_k/2\mathcal L_k\). For \(j\in A_k\), put
$$
k_j=|\lbrace x\in A_k:2j-x\in A_k\rbrace|.
$$
The map \((j,x)\mapsto(x,2j-x)\) bijects the oriented row entries with the ordered same-parity pairs in \(A_k\). Both directions use (10), and diagonal pairs are included. Cauchy--Schwarz, first on parity counts and then on the \(M_k\) centers, gives
$$
\sum_{j\in A_k}k_j=\sum_u M_{k,u}^2
\ge\frac{M_k^2}{2^{h_k}},\qquad
\sum_{j\in A_k}k_j^2
\ge\frac1{M_k}\left(\sum_{j\in A_k}k_j\right)^2
\ge M_k^3 4^{-h_k}.
\tag{11}
$$
There has been no upper bound on any \(M_{k,u}\).

Global affinity gives \(w_xw_{2j-x}=w_j^2\) for every full reflected pair. If \(x\in\widehat R_j\), the defining equality \(w_x=w_j\) therefore also gives \(w_{2j-x}=w_j\). This proves symmetry, the presence of the central atom, and zero score. For \(j\in A_k\) it gives \(\widehat H_p(j)=t_k k_j\) and \(\alpha_k=M_k t_k\). Thus (11) implies
$$
\sum_{j\in A_k}p_j\widehat H_p(j)^2
=t_k^3\sum_{j\in A_k}k_j^2
\ge\alpha_k^3 4^{-h_k}.
\tag{12}
$$
Summing (12) over all levels proves the first inequality of (3), with all original center masses and all central row entries retained. The rank bound proves the second. Jensen applied to the \(m\) masses summing to one gives \(\sum_k\alpha_k^3\ge m^{-2}\), proving the last. These implications prove (4), since \(m^2\le4^{n-h+r}\) under its last condition. If \(r=0\), every realized log-weight difference vanishes, which is equivalent to uniformity; then there is one level, of dimension \(h\) and mass one. Conversely a uniform law has \(r=0\). If \(h=0\), a nonempty finite set of affine dimension zero is a singleton, whose sole row has mass one. This proves all the stated degenerate cases.

For completeness, the raw-weight energy is exactly
$$
\widehat b(p)=\frac1{Z^3}\sum_{j\in A}w_j
\left(\sum_{x\in\widehat R_j}\sqrt{w_xw_{2j-x}}\right)^2.
\tag{13}
$$
The original normalizer is therefore unchanged, as in the full-row normalization of 445a9e668ee1a705 and the selected normalization of 4e2de5c00a49d7b9.

Now fix the heterogeneous product (5). For a supported center \(J=(j_1,\ldots,j_L)\), take the selected product row
$$
\widehat R_J=\prod_i\widehat R_{i,j_i},\qquad
\widehat H_P(J)=\sum_{X\in\widehat R_J}\sqrt{P_XP_{2J-X}}.
$$
It contains \(J\), is symmetric about \(J\), and every retained \(X\) has \(P_X=P_{2J-X}=P_J\), since these equalities hold blockwise. Factoring the finite sums gives the exact identities
$$
\widehat H_P(J)=\prod_i\widehat H_{p_i}(j_i),\qquad
\sum_JP_J\widehat H_P(J)^2=\prod_i\widehat b(p_i).
\tag{14}
$$
These are reflected-energy identities, not depth or moment tensorization.

Every closed ambient halfspace containing \(J\) contains at least one endpoint of every noncentral pair \(X,2J-X\) in \(\widehat R_J\). Indeed, strict exclusion of both endpoints by its defining linear inequality would strictly exclude their midpoint. The central atom belongs to the halfspace too. Equal endpoint probabilities therefore give
$$
P(\mathcal H)\ge\tfrac12\widehat H_P(J),\qquad
\tau_P(J)\ge\tfrac12\widehat H_P(J).
\tag{15}
$$
The oriented row counts a noncentral orbit twice and the central atom once; its factor \(1/2\) uses at most the available original mass in every orbit. Boundary atoms and lower-dimensional supports cause no exception. This is the zero-score specialization of the actual ambient reflection argument in 445a9e668ee1a705.

Square (15), sum with the original center probability \(P_J\), and use (14). This proves the first inequality of (6). For every \(s\ge2\), Jensen on the original probability space gives
$$
M_s(P)=\mathbb E_P[(\tau_P^2)^{s/2}]
\ge M_2(P)^{s/2}.
$$
Together with (3), this proves (6)-(7). If (8) holds, then \(\prod_iE_i\ge4^{-N}\), proving all the stated absolute-coefficient conclusions. The coarser product budget and per-factor capacity conditions follow from (3). Unlike multiplying one-factor actual moment bounds, (14)-(15) incurs one factor \(1/4\) in the second moment and one factor \(1/8\) in the third, for the entire product.

If \(m=4\), then \(r\ge1\) because the law is nonuniform. If \(r\ge2\), one has \(n-h+r\ge2\), and hence \(4\le2^{n-h+r}\). The same inequality holds when \(r=1\) and \(h\le n-1\). Thus only \(r=1,h=n\) can fail this automatic four-level certificate. In that case (3) gives \(\widehat b(p)\ge4^{-(n-1)}\sum_k\alpha_k^3\), which is at least \(4^{-n}\) if the indicated sum is at least \(1/4\). The estimate with the actual \(h_k\) can only be stronger. Accepted fact e8b4bb5731028000 covers heterogeneous products of factors with at most three weights under a parity-occupancy bound of two. The present four-level arithmetic-rank conclusion uses a different sufficient mechanism and has no occupancy assumption; it supplies no claim that all supports admit such a factorization.

To prove the rank-one representation, the image \(\boldsymbol\ell(\Gamma)\) is finitely generated and has rational rank one. Choose a nonzero real number in its rational span and express all its finitely many generators as rational multiples of that number. Clearing denominators and taking the greatest common divisor of the resulting integer coefficients shows that the image is exactly \(\delta\mathbb Z\) for a unique \(\delta>0\). Therefore \(\varphi(v)=(\boldsymbol\ell\cdot v)/\delta\) is a surjective homomorphism \(\Gamma\to\mathbb Z\), proving (9). Its real-linear extension to \(\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\Gamma\) is \(\boldsymbol\ell/\delta\), so its levels on the support are actual affine sections. Since the differences \(x-a_0\) generate \(\Gamma\), the integers \(\varphi(x-a_0)\) generate \(\mathbb Z\). With \(a_0\) in the minimum level and four distinct values, this is precisely the assertion that the values are \(0,\zeta_1,\zeta_2,\zeta_3\), where \(0<\zeta_1<\zeta_2<\zeta_3\) and \(\gcd(\zeta_1,\zeta_2,\zeta_3)=1\).

There is no forced normalized triple: on the complete support \(\lbrace0,e_1,e_2,e_3\rbrace\subset\mathbb Z^3\), the affine field \(\delta(\zeta_1,\zeta_2,\zeta_3)\) realizes any such triple. Nor is \(\varphi\) necessarily integer valued on the saturated intrinsic lattice with this same \(\delta\). For an explicit four-level example, take
$$
A=\lbrace0,e_1,e_2,(1,1,2)\rbrace\subset\mathbb Z^3,
\qquad \boldsymbol\ell=\delta(1,2,1/2),\quad\delta>0.
$$
This is the complete lattice support of its convex hull. To check it, write a point of that tetrahedron with last coordinate \(z\) using the barycentric coefficient \(t=z/2\) of \((1,1,2)\). Its first coordinates satisfy \(x\ge t\), \(y\ge t\), and \(x+y\le1+t\). For an integer point with \(z=1\), these inequalities require \(x,y\ge1\) and \(x+y\le3/2\), which is impossible. At \(z=0\) the only integer points are \(0,e_1,e_2\), and at \(z=2\) the only point is \((1,1,2)\). The four log-weight differences are \(0,\delta,2\delta,4\delta\), and
$$
\Gamma=\mathbb Ze_1+\mathbb Ze_2+2\mathbb Ze_3,\qquad
\varphi(v)=v_1+2v_2+v_3/2.
$$
This height is primitive on \(\Gamma\), but its unique real-linear extension is not integer valued at \(e_3\) in the saturated lattice \(\mathbb Z^3\). An ambient primitive integral height can be obtained here by changing the scale to \(\delta/2\); its support heights become \(0,2,4,8\), whose differences no longer generate all of \(\mathbb Z\). Thus the two normalizations must not be identified.

Lastly, changing the field while keeping every old level requires the change to annihilate every difference of two points in each old level. An arbitrary field perturbation need not satisfy these constraints and can split a level, changing both its dimension and its mass. Nothing in the argument makes such a perturbation. Passing only to the height values in (9) also loses the original geometry of containing ambient halfspaces, so it is not a replacement for the reflection proof on the unchanged support. Finally, the hypothesis \((\mathrm H_{3,N}(\kappa_N))\) of c5f6533ba1c11991 quantifies over every complete convex lattice support and every affine field. The capacity or product-energy criteria proved here do not hold by assertion for all those laws, and no reduction of the universal class to this certified class is supplied. Its locked-target implication therefore remains conditional.
statement:
Let \(n\ge1\), let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex, and suppose that \(A=Q\cap\mathbb Z^n\) is finite and nonempty. Let
$$
w_x=\exp(c+\boldsymbol\ell\cdot x),\qquad
Z=\sum_{x\in A}w_x,\qquad p_x=w_x/Z
\quad(x\in A),
$$
where \(c\in\mathbb R\) and \(\boldsymbol\ell\in\mathbb R^n\). Extend \(p\) by zero off \(A\). No bound is imposed on the number of support points in a parity class. Fix \(a_0\in A\), and define
$$
\begin{aligned}
h&=\dim(\operatorname{aff}A),&
\Gamma&=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Z}\lbrace x-a_0:x\in A\rbrace,\\
r&=\dim_{\mathbb Q}\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q}
\lbrace\log(w_x/w_{a_0}):x\in A\rbrace.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
$$
Thus \(\Gamma\) is the support-generated difference group, in the convention used in accepted fact 1208ab7bdf43319c. It need not be the saturated intrinsic lattice. The number \(r\) is arithmetic rank, rather than the real rank of the functional \(v\mapsto\boldsymbol\ell\cdot v\).

Let \(A_1,\ldots,A_m\) be the nonempty exact weight levels, let \(h_k=\dim(\operatorname{aff}A_k)\), and let \(\alpha_k=\sum_{x\in A_k}p_x\) be their original masses. Retain the full reflected row and score of accepted fact 445a9e668ee1a705,
$$
R_j=\lbrace x\in A:2j-x\in A\rbrace,\qquad
Y_j(x)=\tfrac12\log(p_x/p_{2j-x}).
$$
Use the same selected-row hats as accepted fact 4e2de5c00a49d7b9:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\widehat R_j&=\lbrace x\in R_j:w_x=w_j\rbrace,\\
\widehat H_p(j)&=\sum_{x\in\widehat R_j}\sqrt{p_xp_{2j-x}},&
\widehat b(p)&=\sum_{j\in A}p_j\widehat H_p(j)^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
$$
In particular the quantity called \(b_{\mathrm{equal}}\) here is exactly \(\widehat b(p)\), not the full-row \(b(p)\) of 445a9e668ee1a705. Every selected row contains its central atom, is symmetric about its center, and has identically zero score. One has
$$
0\le r\le h,\qquad h_k\le h-r\quad(1\le k\le m),
$$
and the original-mass energy estimate is
$$
\widehat b(p)
\ge E_{\mathrm{lev}}(p):=\sum_{k=1}^m\alpha_k^3 4^{-h_k}
\ge4^{-(h-r)}\sum_{k=1}^m\alpha_k^3
\ge\frac{4^{-(h-r)}}{m^2}.
\tag{3}
$$
Consequently each of the following is sufficient for \(\widehat b(p)\ge4^{-n}\):
$$
E_{\mathrm{lev}}(p)\ge4^{-n};\qquad
4^{n-h+r}\sum_k\alpha_k^3\ge1;\qquad
m\le2^{n-h+r}.
\tag{4}
$$
Here the three conditions are listed in decreasing strength of the information retained: the last implies the middle, which implies the first. The case \(r=0\) is precisely the uniform law, so \(m=1\) and \(\widehat b(p)\ge4^{-h}\). If \(h=0\), then \(A\) is a singleton, \(r=0\), and \(\widehat b(p)=1\).

For the product conclusion, let \(L\ge1\) and let \(p_i\), for \(1\le i\le L\), be arbitrary laws satisfying the preceding hypotheses in their own ambient dimensions \(n_i\ge1\). Give all preceding objects a block index \(i\), put \(E_i=E_{\mathrm{lev}}(p_i)\), and retain exactly the original laws and normalizers:
$$
P=\bigotimes_{i=1}^L p_i,\qquad
P_X=\frac{\prod_i w_{i,x_i}}{\prod_i Z_i},\qquad
N=\sum_i n_i.
\tag{5}
$$
The arithmetic ranks \(r_i\) in this theorem do not denote the maximum row cardinalities called \(r_i\) in 445a9e668ee1a705; those cardinality parameters and that fact's incidence prices \(\Gamma_i\) are not used. In the actual ambient closed-halfspace conventions of that fact, define
$$
\tau_P(J)=\inf_{\substack{\mathcal H\subseteq\mathbb R^N\text{ closed halfspace}\\J\in\mathcal H}}P(\mathcal H),
\qquad M_s(P)=\sum_JP_J\tau_P(J)^s.
$$
Then
$$
M_2(P)\ge\frac14\prod_i\widehat b(p_i)
\ge\frac14\prod_i E_i,
\qquad
M_3(P)\ge\frac18\left(\prod_i\widehat b(p_i)\right)^{3/2}
\ge\frac18\left(\prod_i E_i\right)^{3/2}.
\tag{6}
$$
More generally, for every real \(s\ge2\),
$$
M_s(P)\ge2^{-s}\left(\prod_i\widehat b(p_i)\right)^{s/2}
\ge2^{-s}\left(\prod_i E_i\right)^{s/2}.
\tag{7}
$$
In particular the exact sufficient energy budget
$$
\prod_i(4^{n_i}E_i)\ge1
\tag{8}
$$
gives \(M_s(P)\ge(1/2)^s2^{-sN}\) for every \(s\ge2\), including \(M_2(P)\ge\tfrac14 4^{-N}\) and \(M_3(P)\ge\tfrac18 8^{-N}\). Thus the common coefficient \(1/8\) works for the two exponents \(2,3\). The coefficient is paid once, independently of \(L\); factors with \(4^{n_i}E_i<1\) are allowed if the other factors compensate in (8). It suffices, in particular, that
$$
\prod_i\left(4^{n_i-h_i+r_i}\sum_k\alpha_{i,k}^3\right)\ge1,
$$
or that every factor satisfies \(m_i\le2^{n_i-h_i+r_i}\).

Every factor with exactly four distinct weights and \(r_i\ge2\) satisfies that last capacity condition. More precisely, a four-level factor can fail to be certified automatically by the last condition of (4) only when \(h=n\) and \(r=1\). Even then, (3) certifies it whenever \(\sum_k\alpha_k^3\ge1/4\), and the finer quantity \(E_{\mathrm{lev}}\) can certify further cases. These assertions impose no separation between weight levels and no parity-occupancy bound.

Finally, if \(r=1\), there are a unique positive generator \(\delta\) of the group \(\boldsymbol\ell(\Gamma)\) and a surjective homomorphism \(\varphi:\Gamma\to\mathbb Z\) such that
$$
\log w_x=\log w_{a_0}+\delta\,\varphi(x-a_0).
\tag{9}
$$
The height \(\varphi\) is primitive on \(\Gamma\). It need not be integer valued on the saturated intrinsic lattice with the same generator \(\delta\). In the four-level case, choosing \(a_0\) in the minimum level yields normalized height values \(0,\zeta_1,\zeta_2,\zeta_3\), where \(0<\zeta_1<\zeta_2<\zeta_3\) are integers and \(\gcd(\zeta_1,\zeta_2,\zeta_3)=1\); no particular triple or arithmetic progression is forced. Formula (9) preserves the weights and levels on the unchanged support. It neither replaces ambient halfspace depth by depth of a one-dimensional pushforward nor permits arbitrary field perturbations while keeping these exact levels. The restricted product conclusions above do not establish the universal arithmetic hypothesis of accepted fact c5f6533ba1c11991 and do not prove the locked conjecture.
